blocks.text:
Day 4 · Breakfast. Full-day tour of Torres del Paine National Park. Soaring almost vertically above the Patagonian steppe, the granite towers of Paine dominate what may be South America’s finest national park. Before its creation in 1959, the area was a large sheep estancia, and it is still recovering from nearly a century of overgrazing, logging and hunting. Beyond the towers lie azure lakes, trails through emerald forests, roaring rivers crossed on swaying bridges and a great radiant blue glacier, from open steppe to rugged mountains topped by looming peaks.

Part of UNESCO’s Biosphere Reserve network since 1978, the park is home to rheas (ñandú), Andean condors, flamingos and many other birds, and to the guanaco, its great conservation success, whose growing herds barely notice visitors. The day begins at the Milodón Cave on Cerro Benítez, 25 km from Puerto Natales, where the remains of a sabre-toothed cat, a native horse and a giant ground sloth, the mylodon, were discovered in 1895; walk for about 30 minutes among its stalactite formations and the life-size replica of the mylodon. In the park, a 15-minute walk leads to Salto Grande, linking Lakes Nordenskjöld and Pehoé, and the return follows the Serrano River and Lakes Toro and Porteño.

blocks.text: Day 5 · Transfer to the bus station and shared bus to El Calafate, then private transfer to your hotel. On Lago Argentino, El Calafate is the gateway to Los Glaciares National Park and its spectacular Perito Moreno Glacier. Stretching some 170 km along the Chilean border, the park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981: about 40% is covered by ice fields, with 47 major glaciers, 13 of which flow east to feed Lake Viedma and Lago Argentino, and some 190 smaller glaciers.
